The other is unaffiliated placement, a real decay whose rate falls over the event (version 2, the owner's correction, [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)). It fails for the other half, since an artwork's order comes from a template, not from an instability (Adams et al.). No thermodynamic quantity is defined. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md) | Participation on a shared canvas thins selectively: people keep coming back while art they invested in survives, so unaffiliated corruption falls over the event and the remaining participants are weighted toward maintainers, a cooling schedule the population produces for itself | The owner's correction to [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md). Over days, random participation is a real decay, and it is not constant. Uninvested participants drop out, and invested ones stay while their art persists, which "creat[es] a survival function that biases towards user's sustaining participation if the art they are invested in persists". So the "temperature" of random corruption is high early and low late. This is a feedback from pattern to flow, and it answers [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) in part. Untested on the logs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-275](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md) | An intervention can come before the interpretation it makes available, so in an organization of processes meaning, policy and influence co-evolve and none of them is simply upstream of the others | A4 §6, on the record's two accounts of emotion, Frijda's appraisal upstream of action readiness and Barrett's construction, and the owner's two replies at U5: "yes, exactly" to "meaning, policy, and influence can co-evolve", and "so much yes" to "An operator may act not because it already possesses an interpretation, but because its intervention creates the conditions under which a particular interpretation becomes available." The first filing left both out. It does not say interpretation never comes first. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-276](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-276.md) | A shared interpretation's coherence, its fidelity to evidence and the plurality of live alternatives are separate quantities, and a population can raise the first while lowering the other two, so a collective interpretation's stability is no evidence of its truth | A1 §6, before the influence canvas: meaning as "metastable patterns of mutually reinforcing constraints", with the caveat that "delusions, dogmas, and self-reinforcing errors can also become metastable". So coherence C(M), evidential fidelity F(M, Y) and plurality P(M) must be measured apart. Zollman's result that sparser communication helps a community settle on the better option ([THEORY-143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md)) and Holman and Bruner's industrial selection ([THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)) are the record's readings that bear on it. It does not say coherence is bad. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md) v3 | Durable authority among an organization's processes need not be a primitive: trust can be the temporal regularity of endorsement that policies earn by being right often, and the same loop entrenches whatever gained influence early | The owner's objection at U5 to A4's call to keep "persistent authority structures" distinct from "transient endorsement updates": "I'd expect persistent authority to be an emergent property here as 'right a lot' policies become distinguished into 'trusted' policies." A5 granted it. Momentary endorsement, established trust and institutionalized authority are regimes of one process, set by how slowly endorsers forget. A5 added the converse: the same loop turns an early lead into durable authority. The claim does not say which of the two a given organization does. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) v4 | An operator framework flexible enough to redescribe any dynamical process explains none of them until it forbids some outcome, and the shared-organization thesis has not yet said what it forbids | A7 §14's own first limitation, which the exchange granted and the record files as the standing objection to the explanatory thesis: "A sufficiently flexible operator framework could redescribe almost any dynamical process. The model must earn its value through restrictive assumptions, predictive compression, and intervention-sensitive predictions." It is [CLAIM-024](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection to the will paper, met by a second account. It is answered by a prediction the framework makes and its rivals do not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-279](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-279.md) v2 | Whether an intervention stabilizes or destabilizes a pattern is relative to a policy and a frame, so denoiser, critic and re-noiser are regimes an operator falls into, not kinds of operator | The owner at U3 proposed operators that may "*re*noise the region it has influence over e.g. because it disagrees with the direction of the current work", and at U5 that named operator types are "just different regimes in the dynamics of our general process", with niches emerging. A5 granted it. A8 grounded it in the owner's r/place case: restoring a pixel is denoising for the group whose image it is and destruction for the group overwriting it. The claim does not say specialization always emerges. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) | A pattern can persist while every constituent is replaced and some constituents work against it, as a high-turnover regime of damage and repair, so the persistence of a product and the persistence of the organization producing it are separate facts | A8 §4 and §9, on the owner's r/place case. An artwork defended for days has its pixels repeatedly replaced, its defenders come and go, and its attackers keep working, yet the image stays recognizable. Its stability is continuous activity, not the absence of it. A8: "the distinction between a persistent product and a persistent producer". An image can outlast the coalition behind it, and a coalition can outlast the images it makes. The claim does not say that the pattern, or the coalition, is a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-281](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-281.md) | Endorsement indexed by role lets a process empower another as a critic while opposing its preferred policy, so an organization that allocates authority by role can keep disagreement working inside it instead of sorting into factions | A2 §8, on the owner's U2 design. If processes endorse only those whose policies match their own, the influence structure "risks degenerating into factions of mutually reinforcing beliefs". Indexing endorsement by role, E_i(j, r, c, t), lets i back j as an error detector without backing j's authority over the final choice. [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) is the worked example. It does not say role boundaries hold under pressure. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) | The precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it are different quantities, and internal conflict is the gap between them | A4 §2, reading Frijda through the record: "control precedence also suggests a useful addition to our parameterization", a priority p_i claimed by a process, which "is not the same as granted influence I_i. An operator can urgently demand control without receiving it. That distinction between *claimed precedence* and *endorsed authority* may be essential to modeling internal conflict." It joins [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) to the endorsement scheme. It does not say which wins. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) v2 | A self, in the self-governing sense, is a historically continuous organization of processes that takes part in governing the conditions of its own persistence, differentiation and transformation, not merely one that persists | A10 §11's central hypothesis, reached after the owner asked at U10 for a research programme on a constitutive theory of selfhood. It treats the endogeneity of governance as the distinguishing mark: the processes do not only run inside an architecture, they change which processes can act and how the organization will operate. A11 named its falsifier. "Self" is in [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s self-governing sense, with persisting and integrated senses nearby, and not the subject sense. Proposed, and under the record's objections: [CLAIM-116](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-116.md), [CLAIM-165](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md), [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) and the counter filed with it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) v2 | An endorsement scheme that denies each operator control over its own authority can make delegation do work: rewarded for how far their preferred policies are realized and not for authority held, operators delegate to aligned others, and the two conditions need not be confined to one-hop allocation | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. A2 made it precise. Two conditions are imposed: each operator's own authority is insensitive to its own endorsements, and its payoff is how closely the collective decision matches what it would endorse. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-286](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) | Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed | A7's central thesis, the explanatory half of the manuscript, kept apart from the constitutive half ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)) as A7 itself asked. Its novelty is the unification, not any ingredient: "multi-agent cognition, competing control systems, temporal discounting, self-exciting processes, and organizational emergence all have substantial literatures". It is the claim [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) objects to. It does not say these processes are a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) v2 | What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation | A6 §7 and A10 §4.3. A6 separated activation continuity, organizational continuity and policy continuity, and put identity in the second: "A dormant coalition can remain available for reactivation because learned parameters, memory traces, and endorsement structures persist." A10 added that continuity of descent "is not automatically an equivalence relation. Organizational histories can branch, merge, and partially overlap." It sits beside [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md), which asks for a coherence measure conserved along a system's own trajectory, and qualifies it for gaps. Its second half is Parfit's branching argument (THEORY-447) applied to organizational continuity. It uses [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s persisting sense. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v2 | A simulation whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed cannot show self-constitution, because the norms the organization appears to maintain are then the modeller's, not set by the organization itself | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. The objection undermines the evidence route; it does not refute the thesis. It is answered if the operators' objectives are themselves produced and revised by the organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) | A record of an inquiry's justifications adds nothing for decisions its current state already suffices for: what it can add is a wider family of decisions for which what is kept suffices, and decisions a bounded agent can make that it otherwise could not | A10's conclusion, with A5's second claim and A10 §5's three values of history: informational, computational and option value. It places [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) without settling it. [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) says what accountable inquiry ought to preserve; this says what preserving it could buy. The cases make the first half exact ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)). The second half, that real inquiries change their questions in ways that make the purchase worth its cost, is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-296](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) | What a system has, what it knows it has, and what it can deploy within a task's deadline are different, and the last is a relation among the resource, the agent, its environment, the task, the deadline and the cue, not a property of any one of them | A18's first candidate, from the owner's EMT case ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)): the drug was stocked, the EMT knew it, and it could not be found before the medic moved on. "If I can't find it, it isn't there" is false of the inventory and right of the decision. [TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md) names the relation. A19 added the cue: the same memory under a different request may retrieve it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) v2 | When an operator's authority is updated by how well it performs on the interpretation it helped make dominant, the coupled meaning and influence of an organization can amplify an initial interpretive advantage without any gain in fidelity to independent evidence | A22's narrow claim and A23 VIII.E's central hypothesis, from the owner's U22: connect retrieval-mediated anchoring to the record's distributed agent as dual meaning and influence canvases ([CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md), [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)). An existence hypothesis until a model ([CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md)) is analysed. If the influence field adds nothing to ordinary adaptive retrieval, [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) stands against it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) v2 | A frame can change a judgement by changing which of an interpreter's stored distinctions are reachable, without supplying any evidence about what is being judged | A20's proposed claim, after the owner tied addressing to anchoring at U20, and A19's "addressing conditions". Its psychological form is the selective-accessibility account of anchoring, and the readings of 2026-10-15 weaken it: Strack and Mussweiler (1997, read) infer accessibility from moderations and latencies without measuring it, and their model lets the same retrieved knowledge push a judgement either way; Harris et al. (2019, read) find the most direct measure of the accessibility step does not replicate and cannot detect priming at all. The retrieval step is inferred, not shown. The mechanism the record holds, attention as sparse distributed memory ([LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)), is a model, not evidence about judges. The extension to communication in general is the record's and is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md) | Iterative retrieval can turn a provisional interpretation into a premise: a framing selects what is encountered, what is encountered reinforces the framing, and the question being investigated drifts as well as the queries | A21's proposed claim, from the owner's U21 link between retrieval-mediated anchoring, agent harnesses and older information retrieval. Classical IR named query drift ([LIT-1079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1079.md)). An agent that rewrites its own task adds [TERM-056](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-056.md), which A21 judged "arguably more consequential". The exchange did this itself between A2 and A13. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) | Filing an argument moves work across time: it is paid for now, in filing, indexing, tracking dependencies and checking it is still current, against reconstruction later, so it is worth its cost only when expected reuse covers it, and recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion | A11, at the owner's request for "content to the effect of computation-storage tradeoffs". A11's four expenditures (materialization, indexing, dependency tracking, refresh) and its break-even condition. The arithmetic is trivial. The thesis is about the record: that its second-occurrence rule ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)) and the nucleation threshold of [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) are approximations to this trade, and can fail in both directions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) v2 | Where reuse cannot be forecast, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is the filing criterion, not only evidence for one: filing once the reconstruction already paid for equals the cost of filing is within twice the hindsight optimum on every sequence of uses, and no deterministic rule without foresight does better, under fixed known costs and with staleness left out | Filed at the owner's request, from the rent-or-buy result of Karlin et al. 1988 ([THEORY-348](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md)) set against [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s clause that recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion. In [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s own terms the break-even rule needs no forecast and is worst-case optimal; [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s second-occurrence rule is that rule when filing costs about one reconstruction. It does not reach staleness, which the theorem forbids rather than prices, or drifting costs, and where reuse can be forecast an expected-reuse rule can do better, so [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion survives there. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-314](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md) | Reusing a filed argument has a recognition cost that a fixed per-use price leaves out: certifying that stored answers cover a new question is NP-complete even for conjunctive queries, grows with the number and size of the stored definitions rather than being a constant per item, and is undefined for an item filed without a statement of what it answers, so each filing raises the cost of later reuse and per-item break-even decisions are not independent | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on answering queries using views (Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava 1995; Chandra and Merlin 1977; Halevy 2001). [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s guarantee needs a fixed, known per-use cost c_a; recognizing that a stored answer covers a new question is a search whose cost depends on everything stored, so filing one item changes the price of using the others. It undermines the premise [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) states, not its arithmetic. The hardness is worst case and over short definitions, partial reuse is cheap, and nothing here is measured on the record. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-315](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md) | In comparative anchoring tasks, considering an anchor shifts the later numerical estimate without adding evidence about the target, and the shift is carried by anchor-consistent knowledge made more accessible; the shift is established, the accessibility step is inferred and has not been measured | The empirical half of [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md), split off under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)'s pilot, which found that claim compound: an empirical claim about judgement tasks and an interpretive extension to communication in general. This half is scoped to the comparative-question paradigm. Its first part is established ([THEORY-337](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-337.md)); its second is the selective-accessibility account ([THEORY-335](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md)), whose direct test failed to replicate with a measure that also missed direct priming. [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) now rests on it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-316](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-316.md) | A person's drive profile is time-indexed: who drives changes with state, such as hungry or sated and stressed or calm, with task and with regime | Split from [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the first of the owner's two parts of 2026-10-11, "'who drives' isn't a constant", stated on its own. It is argued from the drive-profile term and the will line's account of which regime is effective, and no observation the record holds estimates a person's drive profile over successive windows, so it is interpretive. The microbiome part, which the reviews support, stays in [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-317](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) v2 | Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide | Split from [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical half of that claim, the sociology of audiences on which its sheaf reading rests. Its evidence is boyd (2008, read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md)), after Meyrowitz (1985), and one documented collapse, [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md). boyd's claims about collapse are documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the Carmichael case reaches the record secondhand, so it stays Proposed. It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-321](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-321.md) v2 | In text-to-image diffusion models each condition of a prompt can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails: benchmarks find single objects rendered almost always and attribute binding and relations failing most, and composing by adding scores does worst on relations | Split from [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical part of that claim, that each condition can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails, documented by GenEval, T2I-CompBench and T2I-CompBench++, by Attend-and-Excite's "catastrophic neglect", and by Composable Diffusion losing to an energy-based baseline on relations. It corroborates [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md)'s derivation without carrying it, and does not say what causes the failures. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md) | Agreement under a probe family is evidence that two objects share structure only to the degree that the family was chosen independently of the comparison and is evaluated on cases it was not chosen on, so a family selected to make two objects look alike shows only that it can be selected | Split from [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): its evidential half, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md)'s exact half shows that agreement on a restricted probe family does not fix identity; this claim draws the rule for reading such agreement as evidence. It is an argument, not a theorem, so it is interpretive. It does not say which probes to choose, or that held-out probes are neutral. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-324](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-324.md) | In the What Survives Translation? exchange, the manuscript drafted straight from the crystallized argument changed the thesis with no turn arguing the move and dropped 24 of that argument's items, none on request, and the second crystallized argument announced its change of question but left items out without saying which had dissolved and which were lost | Split from [CLAIM-178](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the documented case on which that claim's normative conclusion rests, scoped to the one exchange it comes from. The evidence is the workbench reconstructions of that exchange (2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). One exchange, read by the record's own readers, so Proposed; it says nothing about drafts in general. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md) v3 | With losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem, D⁺_Q(U → V; π), is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source in Blackwell's order over finitely many states, and has A86's D_Q, with the identity on tasks, as its symmetrization | Split from [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the properties of the restated decision term, which [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) called "elementary and checkable", stated on their own so that their warrant can be. Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺. A garbling never gains; with Q all finite problems and π all priors, the term vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by the Bayes form of Blackwell's theorem for finitely many states ([THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)); it is directed; and A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. It does not say this is the right decision term, which is [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s proposal, and it does not state the prior-free relation to Le Cam's deficiency. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). Three stages: an observer finds a stable statistic of fast interactions; members recognize it and use it; their use preserves or regenerates it. Only the third makes the variable an endogenous level. It is the general form of [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md), where trust is the temporal regularity of endorsement that then steers endorsement. It does not say that such a variable individuates one collective: five slow variables sharing a referent may be five processes. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-328](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-328.md) | When the continuities that ordinarily come bundled in a collective (legal franchise, civic role, interpersonal transmission, narrative and place) are separated, several later collectives can each be a genuine successor of the earlier one in a different respect, without any of them, or the earlier collective, having branched in numerical identity | A4's H5 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, in its weak form, on the Washington Senators. The league's successor to the original club is the Twins; the city's is the expansion Senators; the city's present team claims its history through place and narrative. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-118](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-118.md) at the owner's word. It concerns plural successor relations, not branching identity, and rests on one documented case with no data on how supporters divided. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) v4 | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). A5: "a system's ability to reproduce itself as the same kind is not automatically sufficient for its numerical persistence as the same individual." The second time the record meets "causal-organizational continuity": [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) noted A10 §4.3's of 2026-10-13 and did not file it. It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v7 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects." A8 took it and qualified it: a market can crash and a stadium can chant in seconds, so timescale is "a facet of organizational level, not ... an ordering that must hold in every case". Simon's near-decomposability already ties weak coupling between blocks to slow aggregate dynamics ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)). The claim does not say that a slow variable is thereby a level, a system or an individual. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-332](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) | A loosely organized population can change what an outside institution does through its members' separately motivated acts of making, selecting and passing things on, without forming a collective intention or judgment, when the organized pattern of those acts, and not only the acts of identifiable individuals, earns its place in explaining the change | A7's "distributed cultural uptake", of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on the owner's Juggernaut case. On A7's ladder (aggregate behaviour, amplification, collective causal efficacy, collective intention, corporate agency) it asserts the third rung and denies that the third needs the fourth. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) at the owner's word, with A7's defeater priced by [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), which A7 said it needed. It does not say the fandom was the efficacious unit. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v6 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The mapping is the assistant's, A6, filed at the owner's request ("address the still open stuff"). At U8 the owner endorsed it as filed ("Yes, as filed"). It reads both lines into [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s operator model. The sharp edge: it says the lines share one model, not that either line's results transfer to the other unchanged. Each mapping is a hypothesis until a result on one line is shown to hold, through it, on the other. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v2 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-339](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-341](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) v2 | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The claim is stated in that model's terms, as [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and in the diachronic form A4 proposed and the owner asked to be filed at U5 ("make the revisions"): a judgement need not produce the observation it judges, but it reshapes the observer that produces the next one. The sharp edge: the synchronic form, in which each judgement produces its own outcome, is not claimed. That is the open route of [TERM-039](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-039.md) and [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md), and the record demoted it once before ([CLAIM-109](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-109.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) v2 | What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available | The assistant's synthesis, A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, filed at the owner's request at U5. Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. The claim does not say action is unimportant, only that it is not what does the anchoring. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-344](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md) | Resolve is a maintained organization of precedence, commitment and revision that keeps a temporally extended policy effective across changes in locally dominant evaluations while keeping the capacity to revise it; mere slowness or persistence is not resolve | The owner's frame, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "I think emergence of "resolve" could be an interesting frame within which to examine our will-organization framework." A37 defined it, and A39 to A47 revised it each turn: retention and revision as separate grades, fragility against rigidity (A41), access against authority (A42), and governance that makes its own repeated exercise unnecessary (A45, A47). The record already holds a theory of resolve, Ainslie's recursive staking of future choices ([THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)); this is its organizational and revisable form, placed in [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md)'s will-organization cell. The sharp edge: the standard for when revision is warranted is not supplied, and is [QUESTION-087](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md)'s open problem. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v2 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) v2 | No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified by the description that preserves it | A21 §18's Candidate 2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, with A21 §5's clause against circularity and A22's Construction C ([CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md)). A21: "no coarse-graining may be treated as generally normatively adequate solely because it preserves organizational stability, predictive accuracy, or aggregate performance." The case is demonstrated: total output preserves an institution's every judgment and merges a member's claim. The general conclusion is interpretive. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s target-relativity carried from individuation to evaluation, and [CLAIM-060](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-060.md) in the language of coarse-graining. Filed in distributed-agency because its case is a whole against its members. The sharp edge: it does not say which target is right, and it denies that the description can settle it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) v2 | An organization's access to a signal, the signal's authority over action, and action on it are separable, and adaptive regulation keeps the first while making the second conditional on evidence; overcontrol, which buys freedom from harmful acts by cutting access or making inhibition unconditional, is a maladaptive regime and not more control, so flexibility is a context-sensitive property of maintained influence relations, not of how much is inhibited | The owner's idea, U42 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A41's line that an organization "could become extremely resistant to internal changes while losing its capacity to learn, correct errors, or act at all": "useful connections to the ACT and DBT frameworks here, which provide us with accounts/ontologies of maladaption and productive flexibility". In A42's form: recognizing a signal, granting it authority and acting on it are three steps; ACT's defusion is a mechanism for [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s decoupling; DBT adds bounded stabilization before correction; RO-DBT names overcontrol as maladaptive. The sharp edge: these are analogies from human treatment, the organizational classes are A42's proposals, not diagnoses, and RO-DBT's own evidence is "promising but not definitive". | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) v2 | Sen's two aspects of freedom divide along the record's line between what an agent can viably reach and the organization that selects among it: viable reachability can stand for the opportunity aspect only through a map from trajectories to valued functionings, which control theory does not supply, and will-organization gives a causal account of part of the process aspect, not of its fairness or legitimacy | The owner's connection, U11 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, quoting A9 and A10 on viable reachability: "This feels reminiscent of ideas from moral philosophy, e.g. Amartya Sen capabilities account." Worked out by A11. Sen's opportunity aspect is what reachability can represent, once a map says which reachable trajectories are valued functionings. His process aspect is in part what will-organization models: whether the agent's own governance selected the outcome. Read first-hand in [NOTE-263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) (Sen's lecture) and [NOTE-259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-259.md) (Robeyns). The sharp edge: reachable states are not capabilities, and an efficacious governance is not a fair or legitimate process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-353](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-353.md) | A will-organization that gives two operators decisive jurisdiction over a pair of options each, respects unanimous preference and admits any profile of operator rankings cannot always choose, and unlike Arrow's impossibility this is not escaped by giving endorsement richer, cardinal or comparable, information, so what distributed governance must give up is jurisdiction, unanimity or the domain, not an informational restriction | From U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17. The owner raised Arrow; A36 answered "Sen's liberal paradox may be even closer than Arrow" and asked whether a will-organization can "guarantee coherent joint decisions while preserving specified domains of constituent authority and respecting unanimous preferences". [THEORY-027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md) says no in general, and its title holds the difference A36 cited without stating: "unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability". So A36's remedy, letting endorsement use richer information, answers Arrow but not jurisdiction. The sharp edge: it holds only if operator jurisdiction is pairwise decisiveness, which [THEORY-027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md) leaves open even for persons. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) v2 | Freedom of will and autonomy come in degrees along several dimensions, among them viable reachability, control cost, robustness to disturbance, governance reconfigurability, revisability and motivational integration, and agents compare by inclusion of what they can viably reach under matched conditions: a partial order with incomparable pairs, not a scalar, and a gradient only of a declared measure | The owner's, U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation", so can the account speak of "gradations (perhaps even gradients/spectra?) of freedom of will/autonomy". The sharp edge: it does not measure metaphysical free will or responsibility, and reachable-set size is not monotone with autonomy, since a precommitment can shrink the set while making an endorsed project realizable. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) v3 | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real | The owner's, U26 and U27 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: at U26 whether, "adopting an illusionist/fictionalist position", the record can make claims about subjecthood; at U27, "illusory binding-type phenomena in distributed agents", starting from the record's emotion material. A26 answered with a selective fictionalism, "the imagined substantial owner, not the organized agent"; A27 located it: "The illusion might concern the owner, not the binding", and an illusion requires "which system constructs or adopts the misleading representation". The two are filed as one claim. It rests on no claim: the organizational-affect claim it would rest on, [CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), is Deferred, and whether that line reopens is the owner's decision, not made here. The sharp edge: it says nothing about whether the integrated state is felt. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". A35 granted it: "Yes, in a qualified but important sense", and weakened the generalization half, since selection is for performance on "the encounters and feedback distribution actually used for updating". It objects in part to [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md): it grants that a modeller-fixed objective does not show self-constitution, and denies that exogenous origin bars a goal from becoming the training organization's own regulation. The sharp edge: the goal belongs to the training organization ([CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md)), not to the network, and nothing here says the network endorses or governs it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v4 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility are not the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. Positive governance regret establishes excess worst-case shortfall relative to the optimum, and can hold while every requirement is met. Neither quantity identifies an obstructing mechanism, a governance failure or active thwarting; governance-induced frustration needs an argument or intervention showing the allocation of influence responsible. A35: "Importantly, these dual multipliers are not endorsement weights." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md) | Learned local accommodation can reduce the amortized cost of recurrent arbitration: where a recurring conflict among an agent's processes admits a stable accommodation, settling it among the processes can cost less over repeated encounters than escalating each instance to a higher-level process that mediates or overrides, though local negotiation and the relations it needs are not free | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "processes which can navigate disagreement amongst themselves require fewer resources from the system than processes which need to activate additional subsystems to resolve disagreement." | [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" A41's answer, condensed: an insider can aim at the organization's future allocation of authority rather than at the present decision, so robustness must protect the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, and the same protection can silence the opposition that corrects the organization, though some safeguards protect both. Insider threats and internal opposition can look alike. The sharp edge: Byzantine fault tolerance protects a fixed specification; this claim is about protecting the capacity to change it, which no protocol of that kind supplies. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." A38 refined it into three effects, (A) enlarged realizable function class, (B) enlarged budgeted reachable set, (C) new internal organization without better attainable outcomes, filed Saxe et al. under C and the random hierarchy model under B, and said A "needs a separately established expressivity restriction". | [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". | [CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md) | Non-domination of an agent's subcomponents is a candidate constituent of authenticity as an organizational achievement, not a sufficient criterion of ownership: higher-level processes need not impose the outcome because the lower-level ones already support it or settle their disagreement among themselves, and a process that rarely decides keeps access to the roles in which it is consequential | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "'authenticity' should be treated as an organizational achievement characterized by non-domination of subcomponents". | [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) v2 | A normative judgment is well-defined only once its relata are fixed (the organization or standpoint it concerns, the standard, the scale and the context), and that dependence does not by itself make it relative: once they are fixed, the judgment can be false | The owner's, U17 and U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe part of what we've elucidated is that normative judgements necessarily rely on contexts and relations?", then "so maybe something like a frame/order/scale/perspectival-relative normative realism?" | [CLAIM-364](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-364.md) v2 | Low supervisory cost cannot show non-domination: processes conditioned never to object also coordinate without override, so whether an organization dominates its processes must be read from what happens when a constituent dissents, and from its history | A45's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against the owner's non-domination criterion ([CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md)) read through its economy: "a system whose subordinate processes have been conditioned never to object might exhibit perfect local harmony", and "A quiet subordinate process isn't necessarily a satisfied one." | [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). | [CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) v3 | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either | The owner's, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe we should focus less on distress and more on frustration". | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater counts a test-passing factor that is "by independent marks, not an agent". The objection does not say [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s test is wrong, only that this route to defeating it is not open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-396](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-396.md) | Directional information measures between reciprocally coupled units follow the path of a one-sided drive rather than the symmetry of the coupling, so the observed direction of information flow does not by itself reveal which way, or whether both ways, the units are coupled | The record's generalization of one study (Das, Manikandan and Banerjee, [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md)) beyond its system, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 as the record's own claim, since the source makes no general claim. | [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v2 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). The record adds what A5 missed: memory is relative to the projection too ([QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md), [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md)). | [CLAIM-402](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-402.md) v2 | Predictive success of a category across contexts warrants treating it as a real effective kind only when the evidence in those contexts does not pass through the category's own use, or when the effect of that use is modelled: a category that speakers or institutions act on can produce the regularities that confirm it, and contexts that share its use are not independent | A27 §1 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U27 ("are we perhaps better positioned now to address [QUESTION-007](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md)? -009? -011? -028?"), after A26 §2's performative toy. | [CLAIM-403](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v3 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." It does not say that every contribution is owed uptake. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v2 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. | [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". A8 §9: "the underlying system is objectively real, while some scientifically meaningful properties of its descriptions are objectively relational." [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) gives the relativity; this claim adds that relativity is not arbitrariness. | [CLAIM-406](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-406.md) v2 | Structural, pre-emptive testimonial injustice has the form of the record's trust loop: an arrangement that decides whose word is sought can keep an early exclusion going through the indicators of competence that only being sought produces, with no continuing prejudiced act; but the loop alone cannot tell perpetuated privilege from merited expertise, because that needs the prejudice condition the dynamics do not contain | The owner's, U24 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on A23's closing thesis: "this seems to me reminiscent of themes in feminist philosophy, e.g. perpetuation of privilege". | [CLAIM-410](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md) v2 | Removing a constraint on an organization's members does not move it along one scale of more or less governance: it changes a profile of who holds rule-making, monitoring, enforcement, appeal and revision, in which the authority the constraint held can be eliminated, distributed or transferred, and the members' first-order options and their share in revising the conditions of their action can move in opposite directions | The owner's question, U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what does this suggest about e.g. "deregulation" as an ideological end?" | [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) v4 | Under the broad, nonphenomenal definition of interpretation the constitutive thesis uses, substantial processing that is not independently shown to be experiential meets the definition, blindsight's apparently unconscious visual discrimination among it, so interpretation alone does not establish experience, and the thesis must say which further organizational properties, if any, make an interpretation experiential | A3's "most serious challenge" to the owner's thesis, which every later reply accepted. | [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) v5 | Experience is constituted by interpretive organization, not produced by it: an appropriately organized process in which signals acquire significance for a system is the experience, so whether a system can have experience becomes whether it can sustain that organization; the illusions and reappraisals that motivate it show that experience is constructed, not that construction is experience | The owner's, U1 and U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-21. A1 asked whether experience is constituted by interpretation or produced by it; at U2 the owner chose "former reading" and named the brain in a vat, the rubber hand illusion and CBT. A1–A7 refined the thesis without changing it. Interpretation is defined without experience, and it is organization, not judgement. The step from organization to experience is an identity to be defended, not a theorem. Its open edge is the sufficiency condition, which [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) presses and [QUESTION-254](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md) asks for. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-413](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md) v2 | Grounding is not a property of an experience but a relation among an interpretation, what it purports to be about, and a process that constrains it independently; in its current, developmental and epistemic senses it comes apart from whether the interpretation occurs, so ungrounded is not unconstrained, and what makes an interpretive organization experiential need not be what makes its contents veridical | The owner's premise at U1, that sensory apparatus is necessary for grounded experience, as A1, A3, A5 and A7 restated it. A1: "grounding is fundamentally relational, whereas interpretation can, in principle, be internally realized." A5, after reading [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md): "Sensory grounding may concern the independence of the constraints on interpretation, rather than the existence of interpretation itself", and "Ungrounded ≠ Unconstrained". A7 separated current, developmental and epistemic grounding. The epistemic sense is [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md)'s, so the claim rests on it. The occurrence half is the owner's. A7: "What makes an interpretive organization experiential is not necessarily what makes its contents veridical." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md) v3 | A person can be organized by a judgement they attribute to a collective that does not hold it: the audience in a self-model can be a false unity as the owner can, and a judgement can shape a person who rejects it, because resisting it makes it consequential | From the owner's U39 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: how an individual's perspective is shaped by "the perception of a plurality of opinion where one may not exist (e.g. because of a loud minority)", and the phrase "I am whatever you say I am". A40 drew the extension of [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md): "The imagined social audience may also be organized into a false unity." The edge: the attributed collective attitude itself is already held (List's falsely attributed common attitudes, [CASE-104](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-104.md)); what is new is its place in a person's own organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-416](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-416.md) v2 | Competing perspectives compete over the tests that measure them as well as under them: success under an evaluative regime is evidence of competence relative to that regime, a fair test need not be neutral across competences, and a perspective that gains influence over the test can change what later success shows | From the owner's case at U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, rival schools of martial arts vying for dominance, and A35–A37's development of it. It is the one mechanism in the second half of the exchange the record did not already hold in some form. The edge: it does not say that tests are unfair or that rules are changed in order to entrench, which A36 kept apart as a further claim needing its own evidence. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v2 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". A31 agreed with a narrowing that this claim keeps. Selfhood "was carrying several explanatory burdens that we can now separate", and the subject sense is "A separate question". The sharp edge is what the replacement must keep apart: a perspective as realized, in one carrier or distributed across several, a recognizable character shared by many, a causal lineage of realizations, and representations of any of these. The exchange ran these together; the claim does not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. A38: "Perspective concerns how a situation becomes meaningful and actionable. Agency concerns how an organized system can make a difference to what happens." The claim takes the half A38 called "substantially safer": not every organization of practical significance is an agent. It leaves A38's other half, that every rich exercise of agency involves such an organization, as open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-419](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) | The record's grammar is fixed at any moment but amendable by decision, and in practice a move that fit no scheme or relation has been treated as a defect of the grammar and answered by amending it, so a move the grammar cannot hold is not only forced or lost; whether every such move is caught is not shown | The owner's, at U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: "when we've encountered representational challenges, we've generally interpreted those as a symptom of a represntational weakness of the record and used that opportunity to mature the luria configuration, featureset, or both." It answers [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md), which had no reply on file, with the record's own decisions as evidence. It narrows [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) rather than defeating it: the record shows moves that were caught and the grammar amended, and one case ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s literature roles) where a recurring move was left in prose. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-420](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-420.md) v2 | A historical figure's influence can persist in three separable ways, as a story about them, as a perspective transmitted from them, and as later organizations that descend from their activity, and causal descent is not perspectival inheritance: a movement founded to oppose someone descends from them without continuing their perspective | From the owner's U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, corrected. The owner contrasted "immortality" through positive influence that reinforces itself across generations with notoriety whose influence is "self-undermining", the figure's story persisting while their perspective does not. A38 corrected the example and declined the tidy mapping of positive to self-reinforcing and notorious to self-undermining. What survives is the distinction: "The persistence of a story about someone is not equivalent to the persistence of that person's perspective." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v2 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. A37 drew the distinction the record's account of perspective lacked, between the conditions under which a perspective is acquired or reproduced and the conditions under which it stays available. The edge: a doorway and a political revolution are not the same kind of forgetting, and the claim says only that both separate a capacity's existence from the availability of the conditions for exercising it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-422](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-422.md) v2 | A successful corrective act, an executable procedure and a maintained organizational capacity are three different things, so an organization can record a correction, even rewrite its rules, without the corrected capacity being maintained | From A24 and A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, on the owner's cases of a fireground mayday that changed a safety culture (U23) and NASA's learning before and after Challenger (U25). A24: "A successful act, an executable procedure, and a maintained organizational capacity are three different things." A25: "Institutional learning is not complete when an organization changes its rules."
