The edge: a recorded correction is evidence of a correction, not of its maintenance. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v2 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". A28 stated the claim in its strongest line. It rests on [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), that higher-level variables are characteristically slower, and denies that slowness alone settles which level governs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-424](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md) v2 | Reflexive governance of an organization's perspectival arrangements, making the conditions that govern its own interpretation, evaluation and action available for effective examination and revision, is a capacity some organizations of perspective have and others lack, not what makes something a perspective or a self; and the capacity to revise those standards is not the capacity to revise them well | A37's definition, from the exchange of 2026-10-22, re-scoping [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md). [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) says that a self, in the self-governing sense, is an organization that governs the conditions of its own persistence. Every reply from A31 on read it as "a proposed special case": a perspective can be reproduced, persist and adapt without governing its own reproduction. The edge is A37's: "the capacity to revise the standards of evaluation is not equivalent to the capacity to revise them well", which keeps [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md)'s objection standing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) | A perspective governs itself with respect to social judgement to the extent that it keeps access to others' judgements of it while making their authority over its conduct depend on their grounds, not on their visibility, repetition or attributed plurality; neither absorbing every judgement nor resisting every one meets this, since both let the judgements set the terms of response | A39's closing thesis and its fourth reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request. A39: "I can recognize the judgment, investigate its grounds, and refuse to let its apparent popularity substitute for its actual credibility." It is [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s keep-access, condition-authority applied to judgements of oneself, with [CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md)'s false audience as what it guards against. The edge: the opposite of conformity is not independence, since resisting every judgement is governed by the judgements as much as obeying them. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-426](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-426.md) | Where a judgement's circulation helps bring about what it says, its visibility, repetition and attributed plurality are evidence about what it will bring about, so the rule that a judgement's authority should come from its grounds and not its visibility holds for judgements of what already is, and not without qualification for judgements of what someone or something will become | The owner, on 2026-10-23, after [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) was filed: "this is reminding me of 'hyperstition'". Land's definition ([LIT-1396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1396.md)): "hyperstitions – by their very existence as ideas – function causally to bring about their own reality." [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) says not to let a judgement's popularity substitute for its credibility. For a judgement whose popularity helps make it true, popularity is evidence, about the future it is helping to make. The claim narrows [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md), it does not reverse it: visibility still does not show what was the case. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-427](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md) v4 | Evidence for the organizational-perspective framework comes in three grades: that different organizations produce the same ordinary behaviour, that they respond differently to independently specified interventions, and that a model representing the coupling of significance, authority and reproduction predicts those responses better than the strongest existing alternatives at matched complexity; only the third bears on the framework's defeater, and no grade counts if success is defined in the framework's own terms | From the exchange of 2026-10-23, "Framework Overview Request": the owner's U3, "what's the value add here? be it achieved or just intended", and U4, on experiments. A3: "Its strongest achieved contribution is conceptual disentanglement", and the test is "whether it changes what we can infer, distinguish, explain, or discover". A4 set the grades and the rule "not to use the framework itself to define experimental success". [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) already meets the first grade for two constructions. Nothing in the record meets the third. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-428](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md) | Material interdependence couples parties' outcomes without fixing the perspective that organizes the coupling: the same dependence can be organized as mutual opportunity, as competitive vulnerability or as coercive leverage, so interdependence makes for peace to the extent that cooperation also changes which interests the parties' institutions recognize and who holds influence over them, and payoff coupling alone does not settle which | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained": the owner's U6, "maybe this is a stretch, but this seems like it could be connected to the hypothesis that trade promotes peace by coupling interests through coupled economies". A6: "economic coupling is not the same thing as cooperative perspectival integration." The claim is the commercial-peace debate read through [CLAIM-429](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-429.md): trade changes the state of a relationship, and the question is when it changes the coupling. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-429](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-429.md) | Where interpretation decides the occasions for cooperation and cooperation's outcomes revise interpretation, an intervention can change the loop's state or its coupling: a favourable exception changes the state and leaves the rule that judges exceptions as it was, while a change in how far outcomes may revise the governing interpretation changes the coupling, and only the second changes how later evidence is taken | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", A5: "One could ask whether a perspectival invitation changes only the initial state of the system, or also changes the coupling parameters—the degree to which cooperative outcomes acquire authority over future interpretations." And: "It is the difference between introducing a positive exception and changing how exceptions are allowed to revise the rule." The owner took the line up at U6. The claim puts it in the terms of the record's coupled meaning–influence model ([CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md), [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-430](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-430.md) | An interaction can make available a way of relating that its participants' operative perspectives did not hold, by giving each a role to enact in it, so that taking part can come before, and help produce, the reinterpretation it later seems to express; whether the change stays with the partner, generalizes to a category, or is reproduced beyond the encounter are further questions | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained": the owner's U2, asking for Franklin's favour to be read as a "perspectival invitation", and U4, connecting it to intergroup contact. A3: "A favor request invites its recipient to enact a relational perspective that may not yet be part of their established way of interpreting the requester." It is [CLAIM-275](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md)'s intervention before interpretation applied between people, and a candidate answer to the first half of [QUESTION-259](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-259.md), how perspectives are generated. The phrase was coined in A3; the record had not used it before. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. The first version said the clinical word adds nothing because a corporation shows only psychopathy's conduct; once the record assigns functional affect ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md)), that premise is gone. What remains is sharper: the reading's distinction between a harm a corporation takes as its own concern (remorse) and a harm it takes only as a threat (fear) may not be drawable for a corporation, whose every concern was installed for its own ends. Velasquez's "as if" ([LIT-1432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1432.md)) in functional form. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v2 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath", filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). On Frijda's account an emotion is an appraisal of an event's pertinence to a concern, eliciting action readiness with control precedence; a corporation has concerns, appraisals and readiness. A harm to others reaches its decisions either as one of its own concerns (procedures, role duties: functional concern and remorse) or as a threat to its other concerns (regulators, markets: functional fear). A corporation with only the second is functionally psychopathic across the construct, not in part. Wells Fargo's sales practices ([CASE-151](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md)) are its documented case. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) | The potential account of valence is an account of goal-conduciveness valence, not of intrinsic pleasantness: on the component process model's separation of levels of valence, the ordering that prevails ranks states by need satisfaction and goal attainment, the potential's strength tracks 'wanting' and its sign tracks goal conduciveness, while 'liking' is a separate appraisal with its own ordering; so the wanting–liking dissociation is two valence systems coming apart, as that separation predicts, and the objection that the account is not about pleasure is conceded rather than answered | The reply the owner asked for, 2026-10-23, to the objection that potential tracks 'wanting', not 'liking' ([CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md)). Shuman, Sander and Scherer's "levels of valence" separate intrinsic pleasantness from goal conduciveness, on Berridge's evidence; Scherer and Moors report that the two have different physiological signatures and combine multiplicatively. The record's ordering is goal conduciveness. The objection is conceded in a principled form: the account covers goal-conduciveness valence, and "hedonic" in the owner's thesis and its term now reads "goal-conduciveness", the owner having made that revision. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-435](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-435.md) | Veit's common currency and ALARM's override are two regimes of one ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory and overriding, so their rivalry over what the first felt valence did becomes the question whether the earliest potential orderings are continuous: in motivational trade-off experiments, a continuous indifference curve between a noxious cost and a resource for Veit, a discontinuity at a threshold beyond which no resource buys the cost for ALARM; only a graded override, deciding at every level of its own intensity, lacks a currency altogether | A consequence of the owner's reframing of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) records that its rivalry with ALARM "would dissolve if ALARM's "100% weight" were recast as a weight in a common currency rather than an override of it." It is recast instead: both are an ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory or overriding, and the trade-off test separates them by continuity. Corrected on reading Debreu before filing: a threshold override still has a (discontinuous) currency; only a graded override has none ([CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md), part 3a). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) | An instantaneous ordering is a common currency on a finite set of options, where every complete preorder has a real-valued representation, but not in general: the lexicographic order on the unit square has no real-valued representation, while a continuous complete preorder on a connected separable space has a continuous one; so admitting an ordering is strictly weaker than admitting a currency, a graded lexicographic override lies in the gap while an exact threshold override does not, a threshold override with a discrimination threshold is a lexicographic semiorder whose choices can cycle and so is no ordering at all, and even where each instant has a currency, successive currencies need not share exchange rates | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. On finite option sets the two coincide at each instant. On a continuum they do not: a graded lexicographic order, one form ALARM's "100% weight" override could take, admits no numerical representation, while a continuous ordering, the form of Veit's proportional trade-offs, admits a continuous one (Eilenberg; Debreu). A threshold override admits a discontinuous one, and one with a discrimination threshold, a lexicographic semiorder, can cycle and admits no ordering at all (Luce; Tversky). Across instants, representations need not be related, so a sequence of currencies need not be one currency. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md) v2 | 'Wanting' and 'liking' are saliences relative to different, overlapping processes, pursuit and consummation, each ranking states by their bearing on its own concerns; valence is then relative to a perspective, every perspective in the negotiation has its own, the system's valence is that of the perspective whose ordering is the negotiation's potential, and ambivalence is strong saliences of opposite sign with no potential absorbing them | The owner's, 2026-10-23: "maybe 'wanting' and 'liking' can be differentiated by characterizing them as saliencies relative to different (possibly overlapping) processes? I'm not sure if this resolves anything, but I think it least positions the wanting-liking distinction closer to the record's account." Worked through the same day. It relativizes valence to perspectives, as Shuman, Sander and Scherer's micro-valences already do, makes the system's valence the prevailing perspective's, and answers two problems the readings of incentive sensitization left open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-439](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-23, as a candidate for when the functional regime of [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) is felt. It extends Brouillet and Friston's distinction ([THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md)), unfelt fluency as a change in precision and felt fluency as a deeper inference about it, from fluency to valence, and Hesp et al.'s affective precision, a belief about how reliable one's own policies are. It is a candidate for [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md)'s open sufficiency condition, for affect only, and it adopts [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md)'s sense of "felt": attended and available, not a further phenomenal fact. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) | An organization's appraisal is the negotiation among its perspectives, a common currency is that negotiation's admitting an ordering of the options it faces, and goal-conduciveness valence is a regime in which an ordering of the organization's own states by their bearing on its maintenance prevails in the negotiation; so valence presupposes frustration, its sign is whether the organization runs ahead of or behind a reference course along the potential ordering, its intensity is how far the negotiation's decisions follow that ordering, and ambivalence, where no ordering prevails, differs from neutrality, where one prevails and the organization keeps to its course | The owner's, 2026-10-23, in the discussion of [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) that followed the corporate psychopathy filing: "what if the 'appraisal' is the process by which competing perspectives negotiate amongst themselves? I think our earlier results equip us to reframe 'common currency' as 'admits an (at least instantaneous) ordering'. we could then formalize a hedonic valence as a circumstance in which a particular kind of ordering dominates the dynamics." Worked through the same day: potential read through Frijda's marks of control precedence, the kind of ordering fixed as one over the system's own states, and five consequences drawn. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md) | Flow tells against the potential account's condition that valence is undefined where no pair is contested: on the record's own account of flow nothing is overridden because an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, yet flow is reported as positive, so either flow's positivity is intrinsic pleasantness and not goal-conduciveness valence, or flow keeps contested pairs its processes settle among themselves, or the positivity comes after the episode and not during it, or the condition is wrong | The assistant's, from the comparison of the record's will and affect lines of 2026-10-23, filed at the owner's direction. [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) explains flow as intrapersonal synchronization in [TERM-050](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md)'s sense: valuations coincide, so nothing needs overriding. [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md) makes goal-conduciveness valence undefined where no pair is contested. Together they make flow's valence undefined, while flow is reported as positive. The report is second-hand: the flow literature is registered unread ([LIT-914](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-914.md)), and that it is positive during the episode, rather than in retrospect, is exactly what is unchecked. Four exits are named; the objection holds until one is shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-442](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-442.md) | Frijda's emotion and the potential account's system valence sit on opposite sides of the gap between the precedence a motive claims and the authority it is granted: an emotion, action readiness claiming control precedence, is a claim, a perspective's valence is read on its claims, and the system's valence is read on what the negotiation grants, so a change in grants with the claims fixed, as mindfulness is said to make, changes the system's valence and leaves the perspectives' emotions and valences as they were | The assistant's, from a comparison of the record's will and affect lines made at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and filed at the owner's direction. [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) splits precedence into what a motive claims and what it is granted. Frijda's emotion ([THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md)) is on the claim side; the potential account ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)) reads valence off grants, the conflicts actually won. The claim resolves the asymmetry by [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md)'s relativity: a perspective's valence is on the claim side, the system's on the grant side. The sharp edge: on this reading suspension changes the system's valence and no perspective's, which is what the mindfulness case must show. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-443](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-443.md) | A learned prior over which processes govern, P(g \| z, H) ∝ exp(βQ(g, z) + b_H(g, z)), its bias b_H trained by reward-modulated Hebbian updates to the relations by which one process recruits or endorses another, is a candidate mechanism for durable authority and for amortized governance; but persistence is not amortization, which is shown only when earlier work replaces later computation, communication or recruitment, and a prior over authority differs from a prior over actions only when what is appropriate changes | The owner's, 2026-10-23, on whether practice could reconstruct relations of practical authority: "what if we just treat this as a kind of momentum term? or like a hebbian prior?" Worked through the same day (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U9–U12). Momentum is read as switching cost, the Hebbian prior as a learned bias over allocations of authority, and two limits are kept: persistence is not amortization, and a prior over authority must be told from a prior over actions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md) v2 | A replicator dynamic on the distribution of authority among an organization's processes is the special case of the meaning–authority–legibility model in which the organization's interpretation is the authority-weighted mixture of its processes' and evidence reaches scoring without a maintained regime of its own; the replicator tools (Bayesian reading, potential and harmonic games, stochastic stability) then apply, and the record's separate interpretation and legibility states earn their place exactly where interpretation departs from that mixture or legibility keeps a memory of past authority | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-24. The owner asked whether the tools of Soma et al. ([THEORY-899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md)), "or from related work", could formalize the record's more abstract version of the dynamics. Their population–policy duality fits the record's authority dynamics with one identification. Read as a reduction, it says what [CASE-124](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-124.md)'s extra states are for. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-445](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md) | A protective regime, in a person, an institution or a system of states, becomes self-maintaining when the interventions it authorizes shift the evidence used to judge its necessity, the authority and resources of those who judge it, the capacities of its constituents or the threat environment itself in ways that favour its continuation; this can happen when the original threat was real and the first protection apt, and it is a failure only where the regime has become less responsive to evidence that it is no longer needed | The owner's, 2026-10-23, on the account of governance-maintained anxiety ([CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)): "this seems like it would also be supported political and social scientific observations about state/societal protectionism". Worked through the same day (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U16) with securitization, policy feedback, emergency powers and the security dilemma. The literatures support components of the mechanism; none shows a single self-confirming loop behind every protective policy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md) v4 | Some persistent anxiety may be governance-maintained rather than belief-maintained: anticipated threat grants defensive processes authority over action, attention and evidence acquisition; under the avoidance that authority selects, the hypotheses that the situation is dangerous and that it is safe predict the same observation, so repeated safety need not correct the threat estimate; relief reinforces the defense without being evidence of danger; and the regime can outlast a corrected belief, its pathology, where present, being defensive authority insensitive to corrective evidence at avoidable cost | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A governance prior can become self-protecting by reducing the access of the processes most likely to provide evidence against it": "I think you may have inadvertently landed on a formalization of anxiety". Worked through the same day (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U14–U15). A candidate account of avoidance-maintained anxiety, not of anxiety in general, filed as a candidate answer to [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md). Its evidence is model-level and adjacent; nothing here measures authority in patients. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-447](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-447.md) | Model-based wanting is a pursuit process's ranking of the futures it predicts under candidate interventions, P(S \| do(a)) against P(S \| do(a₀)), while cue-triggered wanting is learned salience that need not compute those futures; a process's causal model, its wanting and its practical efficacy are separable, so learning to want differently, learning that a want will not pay, and learning not to act on it are three different changes | The owner's, 2026-10-23, asking what the record's account of wanting is: "i just found myself characterizing it as a kind of a prediction about a future state, and realized that really this is a do() operation and the future state that's being anticipated is what might or might not happen given a candidate intervention." Worked through the same day (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U6–U7).
